transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jasper Li (Redwood SE), Rina Gomez (Redwood SE), Elena Ruiz (CTO, Orchid), Samir Khan (Platform Eng), Priya Menon (SRE), Leo Park (Architect)

Summary:
Quick discovery on integration approach: customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private, wants to understand SDK options (LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations), recommended gateway/proxy pattern, rate limiting and quota enforcement, and observability hooks (traces, token-level cost breakdowns). They want a low-friction pilot and clear next steps for security review.

Topics Covered:
- SDK support and example stacks (Node/Python, LangChain, LlamaIndex)
- Gateway/proxy options (edge proxy vs sidecar vs host gateway)
- Rate limits / quotas and token-level enforcement
- Observability hooks: tracing, token-cost attribution, per-route dashboards
- Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs (latency, cost, data residency, KMS)

Timestamps / Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for carving time, I'm Maya from Redwood, along with Jasper and Rina on the solutions team. How are you all?
[00:08] Elena Ruiz: Good thanks, excited to dig in. We've been doing some internal prototyping and want to verify how Redwood would sit in our stack.
[00:18] Jasper Li: Great, can you give a quick picture of your current flow? SDKs uh, or are you using a gateway today?
[00:26] Samir Khan: Sure. Right now we have a kube-based API gateway (NGINX + envoy) fronting our services. Our LLM calls are going through a small sidecar that fans out to a managed model host (not Redwood). We're testing LangChain for orchestration and LlamaIndex for embeddings/FAISS.
[00:41] Priya Menon: And we need per-tenant quotas, like token budgets per project, and we need to cap rps on certain routes. Also, observability: our SREs want token-level cost attribution mapped to traces.
[00:54] Maya Patel: Ok makes sense. On SDKs: Redwood has first-class SDKs in Node and Python, and we provide examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. We also have middleware you can drop into your existing gateway or use Redwood's client-side SDK to call directly.
[01:10] Leo Park: How opinionated is the SDK? We're worried about vendor lock with the LangChain chains since we have custom prompt templates.
[01:18] Rina Gomez: The SDK is intentionally thin. It exposes streaming, function/tool call semantics, and structured outputs. For LangChain we have example connectors and a small utility that maps chain calls to Redwood streaming tokens but you keep control of the prompt templates; there's no forced chain shape.
[01:34] Samir Khan: Can you integrate with our envoy sidecar or do we need to rework to use a gateway?
[01:41] Jasper Li: You have options: 1) call Redwood directly from your application / SDK; 2) put a Redwood-aware gateway or proxy in front that handles auth, rate-limit and route mapping; 3) run a tiny sidecar that wraps the SDK for each pod. The proxy path is popular for centralized quotas. Sidecar approach gives lower per-request latency but higher ops overhead.
[02:02] Elena Ruiz: On latency - our SLAs are 200ms tail for short completions. Does Redwood hit that on hosted?
[02:09] Jasper Li: For short context models we can meet 200ms p50 on hosted in many regions; p95 depends on model and prompt length. Dedicated with pinned capacity reduces tail latency and jitter. Private on-prem gives you the most control but needs network and infra ops to tune.
[02:27] Priya Menon: What about caching? We do a lot of retrieval-augmented generation, so KV/prefix cache on the model side would help.
[02:35] Rina Gomez: We support both KV cache and prefix caching on the runtime; plus you can enable automatic prefix caching for repeated prompts. That reduces token spend and improves latency for repeated patterns. We'll show cache hit/miss metrics in the console.
[02:50] Samir Khan: Observability hooks - can we get spans that include token counts and costs?
[02:55] Jasper Li: Yes, we emit trace spans that include token counts, model version, and an estimated token cost. You can push traces to your tracing backend via OTLP or use Redwood's console which surfaces token-level cost and per-route latency.
[03:08] Elena Ruiz: Do you have examples for hooking into Datadog and Jaeger?
[03:12] Rina Gomez: We have docs and example config for Datadog, Grafana Tempo, Jaeger. It's OTLP compatible so you can route to your existing tracing pipeline.
[03:22] Leo Park: On auth - SSO and SAML for console access, and programmatic keys for SDKs. We need audit logs to satisfy security audits.
[03:31] Maya Patel: Redwood supports SSO (SAML/OKTA), RBAC with fine-grained roles, and audit logs with retention options. For Private deployments we support KMS integrations (customer-managed keys) and HSMs in some on-prem setups.
[03:45] Samir Khan: And data residency? We host customers in specific regions?
[03:49] Jasper Li: For Hosted we have region controls; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity in chosen regions; Private gives you full control over where models/processes run. We can discuss specific region guarantees if that's a blocker.
[03:58] Priya Menon: Rate limiting - we need per-tenant token budgets and hard caps when exceeded with graceful 429 responses and circuit fallbacks. Can Redwood enforce that at the gateway?
[04:10] Jasper Li: Yes, Redwood supports per-api-key quotas and per-route rate limits. For more complex policies you can use our policy engine to configure burst windows, token-level budgets, and automatic fallback to smaller model variants. If you put a proxy in front we can supply a sidecar or middleware that enforces local pre-checks before hitting the network to avoid wasted tokens.
[04:32] Elena Ruiz: If the proxy enforces pre-checks and returns 429, is the request counted for billing?
[04:39] Rina Gomez: If the request doesn't reach the model (blocked locally), there's no model token charge. If it reaches Redwood but model returns an error, billing may depend on how far the model executed; we'll show exact accounting in billing logs. We recommend the proxy pre-checks for cost predictability.
[04:57] Samir Khan: Pilot scope - we'd like Redwood hosted for initial pilot, then evaluate Dedicated or Private if latency/cost or compliance requires it. Pilot duration 6 weeks with 2 models: short completion model and larger chat model for contextual responses.
[05:12] Maya Patel: Sounds good. For the benchmark we'll need your sample traffic and prompt templates. Jasper can run hosted + dedicated sim to show latency and cost delta.
[05:21] Jasper Li: I will also include a gateway pattern doc: envoy config snippets, sidecar example, and a webhook-based quota pre-check pattern.
[05:31] Priya Menon: Any open-source references? We use LangChain heavily and LlamaIndex for retrieval, do you have tested adapters?
[05:38] Rina Gomez: Yes, adapters exist. For LangChain we have example chains and a community repo. For LlamaIndex we have an integration that maps index queries to embeddings and stores vectors in your existing vector DB. Expect slight naming issues in auto transcripts (sometimes it shows LamaIndex).
[05:54] Elena Ruiz: Compliance/Docs - we need SOC2 + pen test + encryption at rest.
[05:59] Maya Patel: We'll send SOC2, ISO docs, and an architecture whitepaper. For Dedicated and Private, we can do a more formal security review.
[06:07] Leo Park: Networking - for Private we need a clear VPC peering / routing checklist.
[06:12] Jasper Li: We'll attach a connectivity checklist: VPC endpoints, firewall rules, DNS entries, and cert rotation notes.
[06:19] Samir Khan: A few quick technical questions: 1) Can you do streaming responses through our gateway without buffering? 2) How do you handle KV cache invalidations? 3) Do you have token-level mutation logs?
[06:30] Rina Gomez: 1) Yes, streaming works end-to-end if your gateway supports chunked transfer encoding; we have examples for envoy. 2) KV cache can be invalidated via API or TTL; we provide hooks to programmatically purge keys. 3) We log token counts per request and can surface diffs for auditing; for full content logs you'd need explicit retention settings due to privacy.
[06:50] Elena Ruiz: Any glaring blockers for us starting a pilot?
[06:53] Maya Patel: Not from our side. You'll need to share traffic profile and any compliance docs. We'll run a small benchmark and iterate.
[07:01] Priya Menon: Pricing - send pilot pricing and a sample Dedicated reservation estimate.
[07:05] Maya Patel: Will do. Also we'll include a sketch of model fallback policies and cost tradeoffs.
[07:12] Jasper Li: I'll record a short demo of envoy config + LangChain adapter and share the repo link.
[07:19] Closing recap by Maya:
- Redwood to send SOC2 + arch docs (Maya)
- SE to run hosted + dedicated benchmarks (Jasper)
- Orchid to provide traffic profile and compliance checklist (Samir / Priya)
- Schedule follow-up network/connectivity deep-dive for Private option

[07:35] End meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hears (LlamaIndex shown as LamaIndex; OTLP sometimes transcribed as "O-T-L-P''). There are overlaps when multiple speakers responded quickly.

Shared artifacts mentioned:
- envoy-config-examples repo (link shared in chat)
- Redwood SOC2 + architecture whitepaper (to be sent)
- Benchmark template spreadsheet (to be used for hosted vs dedicated runs)
